title: Finding Sine and Tangent from Cosine in Quadrant II
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given that \cos x = -5/13 and x \in [\pi/2, \pi], find the exact values of \sin x and \tan x.

steps.title: Apply the Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Substitute cos x = -5/13 into sin^2 x = 1 - cos^2 x to obtain 144/169.
steps.why: The square of -5/13 is 25/169, and subtracting from 1 gives 144/169.

steps.title: Choose the Positive Root for Quadrant II
steps.explanation: In Quadrant II, sin x is non-negative, so taking the principal square root yields sin x = 12/13.
steps.why: The vertical coordinate sin x on the unit circle is positive for angles between pi/2 and pi.

steps.title: Compute Tangent
steps.explanation: Divide sin x = 12/13 by cos x = -5/13 to obtain tan x = -12/5.
steps.why: By definition, tan x = sin x / cos x.
